3. COOPERATIVE HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT

The Kano Solar Cooperative (KSC) was founded in early 2019 by a group of 23 residents and small business owners from the Gidan Wuta, Dakata, and Kawaji areas of Kano Municipal. The founding members were united by a common interest in addressing the chronic power supply challenges in their neighbourhoods and exploring solar energy as a viable alternative.

Initial activities, between March 2019 and December 2020, focused on member education, bulk procurement of solar home systems, and the installation of small-scale solar units for individual households. During this period, the Cooperative facilitated the installation of over 200 solar home systems for its members through negotiated supplier arrangements.

In 2021, the Cooperative secured a grant from a national renewable energy development programme to support the establishment of a community-owned microgrid. Following technical feasibility studies and community consultations, construction of the Gidan Wuta Microgrid commenced in November 2021 and was completed in April 2022. The microgrid was formally commissioned on 22 May 2022 by the Kano State Commissioner for Commerce, Industry, Cooperatives and Tourism.

Since commissioning, the microgrid has undergone several upgrades, including the addition of a battery storage bank in early 2024 and the expansion of distribution lines to cover an additional 45 households in the Kawaji extension area. As at the date of this profile, the Cooperative continues to operate the microgrid as its primary asset, with all operational decisions overseen by the Board and technical management team.

4. MEMBERSHIP

4.1 Membership Strength
As at 30 June 2025, the Cooperative has a total of 187 registered members, comprising:
- Individual members: 152
- Small business members: 28
- Institutional members (including two community schools and one primary health centre): 7

4.2 Membership Criteria
Membership is open to any person of good character residing or carrying on business within the Cooperative's operational area, subject to the payment of the prescribed share capital and admission fees. The current share capital requirement is ₦5,000 per member, payable in instalments where necessary.

4.3 Membership Records
The Register of Members is maintained at the registered office and updated quarterly. Members are required to notify the Secretary of any change of address or contact details within 30 days.

---

5. OPERATIONAL OVERVIEW

5.1 Core Asset
The Cooperative's principal asset is the Gidan Wuta Microgrid, a solar-powered community microgrid with a peak generation capacity of 85 kW. The microgrid serves approximately 210 connections, comprising residential, commercial, and institutional customers within the Gidan Wuta and adjacent areas.

5.2 Services Provided
- Supply of electricity to connected customers on a prepaid metering basis
- Sale and installation of solar home systems and accessories
- Maintenance and repair services for solar equipment
- Community education and awareness programmes on renewable energy

The affairs of the Cooperative are managed by a Board of Directors comprising seven (7) members, elected at the Annual General Meeting for a term of three years. The Board as at 30 June 2025 is constituted as follows:

6.2 Board Resolutions
At its meeting held on 14 April 2025, the Board passed the following resolutions, extracts of which are recorded in the minutes of that meeting:

Resolution 2025/04/01: That the Cooperative adopts a new maintenance reserve policy, setting aside a minimum of 12% of monthly revenue from electricity sales into a dedicated maintenance reserve account, to be used exclusively for the repair, replacement, and upgrade of microgrid assets.

Resolution 2025/04/02: That the Board approves the engagement of two additional technical staff, to be recruited on a rolling basis through the second half of 2025, subject to the availability of funds and satisfactory performance of the existing technical team.

Resolution 2025/04/03: That the Cooperative shall pursue a partnership with the State Ministry of Rural Development for the extension of the microgrid network to the Unguwar Dawa settlement, with the Ministry expected to contribute toward the cost of distribution infrastructure.

The Cooperative is also registered with the Federal Ministry of Power for participation in the rural electrification programme, under the reference number FMP/REP/2021/038.

7. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING NOTES – 2025

The 7th Annual General Meeting of the Cooperative was held on 28 June 2025 at the Community Hall, Gidan Wuta. The meeting was attended by 143 members in person, with an additional 22 members participating by proxy. The following is a summary of the key items discussed and decisions taken:

7.1 Chairman's Address
The Chairman, Alhaji Musa Abdullahi Gambo, welcomed members and reported on the Cooperative's activities over the preceding year. He noted the successful completion of the battery storage bank upgrade in early 2024 and the expansion of distribution lines to the Kawaji extension area. He also highlighted the Cooperative's commitment to improving service reliability and reducing downtime, particularly during the harmattan season when dust accumulation affects solar panel output.

7.2 Financial Report
The Treasurer, Mrs. Grace Okafor, presented the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The Cooperative recorded a surplus of ₦2,847,500 for the year, compared with a surplus of ₦1,963,200 in the previous year. **3.2 Battery Bank 1 – Cell Configuration and Ratings**

The battery bank consists of 120 cells of 2 V nominal voltage each, arranged in a single series string. Each cell has a rated capacity of 100 Ah at the 10-hour discharge rate (C10). The total nominal energy capacity is therefore 120 × 2 V × 100 Ah = 24,000 Wh = 24 kWh. **Correction (16 August 2023):** The above calculation is incorrect. The cell capacity is 100 Ah at 2 V, which gives 200 Wh per cell. With 120 cells, the total is 120 × 200 Wh = 24,000 Wh = 24 kWh. This is the cell-level capacity, not the system-level capacity. The system-level capacity is rated at 200 kWh, which accounts for the full DC system voltage and the usable energy at the C10 rate. The 200 kWh figure is the manufacturer's rated capacity for the complete bank as configured. This correction is noted in the margin of the original commissioning sheet.

**3.3 Battery Bank 1 – Performance and Operational Notes**

- The battery bank is charged by the two solar PV arrays (Array A and Array B) through the Sungrow hybrid inverter. The inverter's charge controller is set to a maximum charge voltage of 264 V DC (2.2 V per cell) and a float voltage of 252 V DC (2.1 V per cell).
- The bank is discharged during evening peak hours (18:00–22:00) to support the community load. The depth of discharge is limited to 60% by the inverter settings to prolong battery life.
- A battery monitoring system (BMS) is installed. The BMS records cell voltages, temperatures, and state of charge. Data is logged every 15 minutes and stored on the local SCADA PC.
- The battery room is ventilated by two exhaust fans. The fans are set to run automatically when the room temperature exceeds 35°C. During the harmattan season (November–February), the fans run more frequently due to higher ambient temperatures and dust.
- The battery bank was inspected on 5 October 2024. All cells were found to be in good condition. The electrolyte levels were checked and topped up with distilled water where necessary. The terminal connections were cleaned and re-torqued to 12 N·m.
- A load test was performed on 12 January 2025. The bank was discharged at a constant power of 40 kW for 4 hours. The voltage remained above 240 V DC throughout the test. The test was terminated after 4 hours as per the test plan. The bank supplied 160 kWh of energy during the test.
- On 3 March 2025, a routine inspection found that cell number 47 had a slightly swollen case. The cell was monitored for two weeks. No further swelling was observed. The cell was noted for closer monitoring during the next quarterly inspection.
- The battery bank is cleaned with a dry cloth every two weeks to remove dust. The cleaning schedule is aligned with the PV array cleaning schedule (see Section 2.7 of this record).

**4.2 Chemistry and Construction**

Battery Bank 2 uses valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA) battery technology with absorbed glass mat
(AGM) separators. Each cell is a 2 V, 1000 Ah (C10) monobloc. The cells are arranged in a single
string of 120 series-connected units, giving a nominal bank voltage of 240 V DC. The AGM design is
maintenance-free in normal operation, but the manufacturer's manual still recommends quarterly
visual inspections and occasional terminal re-torque checks, which are followed at this site.

The cells are installed in four steel racks, each holding 30 cells. The racks are painted with
acid-resistant epoxy. The cells are oriented with the terminals facing the aisle for easier access.
The rack layout is shown in the as-built drawing attached to the commissioning report (drawing
number GW-MG-EL-014, revision B).

The bank is fitted with a battery management system (BMS) supplied by Hunan GeePower. The BMS
monitors individual cell voltages, string current, and cell temperatures. The BMS communicates
with the Sungrow hybrid inverter via Modbus RTU on the local SCADA network. The BMS settings are
listed in Section 4.5.

**4.3 Installation and Commissioning Notes**

Installation work began on 10 February 2024 and was completed on 14 February 2024. The
commissioning test was carried out on 21 February 2024 by a team from the Kano Solar Cooperative
with technical support from the supplier's field engineer. The following tests were performed and
recorded in the commissioning report (GW-CR-2024-002):

- Insulation resistance test: measured 2.4 MΩ at 1000 V DC between the bank terminals and earth.
  The pass criterion was >1 MΩ.
- Open-circuit voltage check: average cell voltage was 2.14 V DC, within the manufacturer's
  tolerance of 2.12–2.16 V DC. The maximum deviation between cells was 0.03 V.
- Capacity acceptance test: the bank was discharged at a constant power of 40 kW. The discharge
  lasted 5 hours and 12 minutes, and the bank supplied 208 kWh of energy. The end-of-discharge
  voltage was 222 V DC (1.85 V per cell). This test confirmed the bank's capacity was above the
  rated 200 kWh at the time of commissioning.
- Charging test: the bank was recharged using the inverter's float/boost profile. The boost charge
  was set at 264 V DC for 6 hours, followed by float at 252 V DC. The charge was terminated when
  the charging current dropped below 2% of the rated current.

The commissioning report noted one minor issue: the torque on the inter-cell connector bolts was
found to be below the specified 12 N·m on six cells. The bolts were re-torqued and the issue was
closed out on the same day.

The data is stored on a local SD card (32 GB) and is also transmitted to

3. COOPERATIVE HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT

The Kano Solar Cooperative (KSC) was founded in early 2019 by a group of 23 residents and small business owners from the Gidan Wuta, Dakata, and Kawaji areas of Kano Municipal. The founding members were united by a common interest in addressing the chronic power supply challenges in their neighbourhoods and exploring solar energy as a viable alternative.

Initial activities, between March 2019 and December 2020, focused on member education, bulk procurement of solar home systems, and the installation of small-scale solar units for individual households. During this period, the Cooperative facilitated the installation of over 200 solar home systems for its members through negotiated supplier arrangements.

In 2021, the Cooperative secured a grant from a national renewable energy development programme to support the establishment of a community-owned microgrid. Following technical feasibility studies and community consultations, construction of the Gidan Wuta Microgrid commenced in November 2021 and was completed in April 2022. The microgrid was formally commissioned on 22 May 2022 by the Kano State Commissioner for Commerce, Industry, Cooperatives and Tourism.

Since commissioning, the microgrid has undergone several upgrades, including the addition of a battery storage bank in early 2024 and the expansion of distribution lines to cover an additional 45 households in the Kawaji extension area. As at the date of this profile, the Cooperative continues to operate the microgrid as its primary asset, with all operational decisions overseen by the Board and technical management team.

The Cooperative's principal asset is the Gidan Wuta Microgrid, a solar-powered community microgrid with a peak generation capacity of 85 kW. The microgrid serves approximately 210 connections, comprising residential, commercial, and institutional customers within the Gidan Wuta and adjacent areas.

7. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING NOTES – 2025

The 7th Annual General Meeting of the Cooperative was held on 28 June 2025 at the Community Hall, Gidan Wuta. The meeting was attended by 143 members in person, with an additional 22 members participating by proxy. The following is a summary of the key items discussed and decisions taken:

7.1 Chairman's Address
The Chairman, Alhaji Musa Abdullahi Gambo, welcomed members and reported on the Cooperative's activities over the preceding year. He noted the successful completion of the battery storage bank upgrade in early 2024 and the expansion of distribution lines to the Kawaji extension area. He also highlighted the Cooperative's commitment to improving service reliability and reducing downtime, particularly during the harmattan season when dust accumulation affects solar panel output.

7.2 Financial Report
The Treasurer, Mrs. Grace Okafor, presented the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. The Cooperative recorded a surplus of ₦2,847,500 for the year, compared with a surplus of ₦1,963,200 in the previous year. Total revenue from electricity sales amounted to ₦8,412,000, while income from the sale of solar home systems and maintenance services contributed an additional ₦1,205,000. Operating expenses, including staff salaries, maintenance costs, and administrative overheads, totalled ₦6,769,500.

**3.2 Battery Bank 1 – Cell Configuration and Ratings**

The battery bank consists of 120 cells of 2 V nominal voltage each, arranged in a single series string. Each cell has a rated capacity of 100 Ah at the 10-hour discharge rate (C10). The total nominal energy capacity is therefore 120 × 2 V × 100 Ah = 24,000 Wh = 24 kWh. **Correction (16 August 2023):** The above calculation is incorrect. The cell capacity is 100 Ah at 2 V, which gives 200 Wh per cell. With 120 cells, the total is 120 × 200 Wh = 24,000 Wh = 24 kWh. This is the cell-level capacity, not the system-level capacity. The system-level capacity is rated at 200 kWh, which accounts for the full DC system voltage and the usable energy at the C10 rate. The 200 kWh figure is the manufacturer's rated capacity for the complete bank as configured. This correction is noted in the margin of the original commissioning sheet.

**3.3 Battery Bank 1 – Performance and Operational Notes**

- The battery bank is charged by the two solar PV arrays (Array A and Array B) through the Sungrow hybrid inverter. The inverter's charge controller is set to a maximum charge voltage of 264 V DC (2.2 V per cell) and a float voltage of 252 V DC (2.1 V per cell).
- The bank is discharged during evening peak hours (18:00–22:00) to support the community load. The depth of discharge is limited to 60% by the inverter settings to prolong battery life.
- A battery monitoring system (BMS) is installed. The BMS records cell voltages, temperatures, and state of charge. Data is logged every 15 minutes and stored on the local SCADA PC.
- The battery room is ventilated by two exhaust fans. The fans are set to run automatically when the room temperature exceeds 35°C. During the harmattan season (November–February), the fans run more frequently due to higher ambient temperatures and dust.
- The battery bank was inspected on 5 October 2024. All cells were found to be in good condition. The electrolyte levels were checked and topped up with distilled water where necessary. The terminal connections were cleaned and re-torqued to 12 N·m.
- A load test was performed on 12 January 2025. The bank was discharged at a constant power of 40 kW for 4 hours. The voltage remained above 240 V DC throughout the test. The test was terminated after 4 hours as per the test plan. The bank supplied 160 kWh of energy during the test.
- On 3 March 2025, a routine inspection found that cell number 47 had a slightly swollen case. The cell was monitored for two weeks. No further swelling was observed. The cell was noted for closer monitoring during the next quarterly inspection.
- The battery bank is cleaned with a dry cloth every two weeks to remove dust. The cleaning schedule is aligned with the PV array cleaning schedule (see Section 2.7 of this record).

capacity at the nominal 240 V DC bus voltage, based on a 5-hour discharge rate (C5) to the
manufacturer's specified end-of-discharge voltage of 1.85 V per cell. The 200 kWh figure is the
current controlled entry for this bank and is used for all energy accounting, inverter sizing
calculations, and performance reporting in this record.

**4.2 Chemistry and Construction**

Battery Bank 2 uses valve-regulated lead-acid (VRLA) battery technology with absorbed glass mat
(AGM) separators. Each cell is a 2 V, 1000 Ah (C10) monobloc. The cells are arranged in a single
string of 120 series-connected units, giving a nominal bank voltage of 240 V DC. The AGM design is
maintenance-free in normal operation, but the manufacturer's manual still recommends quarterly
visual inspections and occasional terminal re-torque checks, which are followed at this site.

The cells are installed in four steel racks, each holding 30 cells. The racks are painted with
acid-resistant epoxy. The cells are oriented with the terminals facing the aisle for easier access.
The rack layout is shown in the as-built drawing attached to the commissioning report (drawing
number GW-MG-EL-014, revision B).

The bank is fitted with a battery management system (BMS) supplied by Hunan GeePower. The BMS
monitors individual cell voltages, string current, and cell temperatures. The BMS communicates
with the Sungrow hybrid inverter via Modbus RTU on the local SCADA network. The BMS settings are
listed in Section 4.5.

**4.3 Installation and Commissioning Notes**

Installation work began on 10 February 2024 and was completed on 14 February 2024. The
commissioning test was carried out on 21 February 2024 by a team from the Kano Solar Cooperative
with technical support from the supplier's field engineer. The following tests were performed and
recorded in the commissioning report (GW-CR-2024-002):

- Insulation resistance test: measured 2.4 MΩ at 1000 V DC between the bank terminals and earth.
  The pass criterion was >1 MΩ.
- Open-circuit voltage check: average cell voltage was 2.14 V DC, within the manufacturer's
  tolerance of 2.12–2.16 V DC. The maximum deviation between cells was 0.03 V.
- Capacity acceptance test: the bank was discharged at a constant power of 40 kW. The discharge
  lasted 5 hours and 12 minutes, and the bank supplied 208 kWh of energy. The end-of-discharge
  voltage was 222 V DC (1.85 V per cell). This test confirmed the bank's capacity was above the
  rated 200 kWh at the time of commissioning.
- Charging test: the bank was recharged using the inverter's float/boost profile. The boost charge
  was set at 264 V DC for 6 hours, followed by float at 252 V DC. The charge was terminated when
  the charging current dropped below 2% of the rated current.

The commissioning report noted one minor issue: the torque on the inter-cell connector bolts was
found to be below the specified 12 N·m on six cells. The bolts were re-torqued and the issue was
closed out on the same day.

**Section 4.5 – Diesel Generator 2 (DG2)**

**4.5.1 General Description**

Diesel Generator 2 (DG2) is the secondary backup generation unit for the Gidan Wuta
microgrid. It is installed in the generator house adjacent to the control room, on the
north side of the battery room. DG2 is intended for emergency standby duty, mainly for
the control room, battery room ventilation, and the water pumping load. It is not
designed for parallel operation with the main grid or with DG1. The unit is equipped
with an automatic mains failure (AMF) panel which starts the generator automatically
when the grid supply fails and the battery state of charge is below 40%.

The generator set was supplied by Kano Solar Cooperative through their approved
vendor, and it was installed by the same team that commissioned the solar PV array.
The installation date is recorded as 14 March 2022. The warranty period is 24 months
from the date of installation, which means the warranty expired on 13 March 2024.
No warranty extension has been applied for, and the unit is now under the standard
maintenance contract with the vendor.

**4.5.3 Installation and Commissioning**

The generator set was installed on a concrete plinth of 150 mm thickness, with
anti-vibration mounts (four mounts, one at each corner). The plinth is located
approximately 1.5 m from the rear wall of the generator house, and the exhaust is
routed through the roof with a rain cap. The exhaust pipe is insulated with fibreglass
wrap for the first 2 m from the turbocharger outlet.

The following ancillary items were installed with DG2:

- Day tank of 250 L capacity (integral base tank). The tank is fitted with a
  mechanical float valve and a sight glass.
- Fuel transfer pump (manual, hand-operated) for filling from the main storage tank.
- Exhaust silencer (industrial grade, 25 dB(A) attenuation).
- Automatic battery charger (3 A, 24 V DC) connected to the control panel.
- Space heater for the alternator (150 W, thermostatically controlled).
- Acoustic enclosure (weatherproof, 1 mm steel) with ventilation louvres.

Commissioning was carried out on 21 March 2022 by the vendor's engineer, Mr. Tunde
Adebayo, assisted by the site technician (Musa Ibrahim). The commissioning report is

The report contains the load test results at 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of the rated

time (approximately 38°C) and the restricted airflow in the generator house. The
vendor recommended additional ventilation louvers on the rear wall, which were
installed in April 2022.

**4.5.4 Charge Controllers**

The microgrid is equipped with three (3) charge controllers, one per PV array
sub-field. The controllers are of the MPPT type, model
SunSaver-MPPT-60A. Each controller is rated for a maximum input voltage of
150 V DC and a maximum input current of 60 A. The maximum output current is
60 A at 48 V DC nominal battery bank voltage.

The serial numbers and installation dates are as follows:

| Controller | Serial Number | Array | Installation Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| CC-01 | SS-MPPT-60A-2214-0871 | Sub-field A (North) | 12 March 2022 |
| CC-02 | SS-MPPT-60A-2214-0872 | Sub-field B (East) | 12 March 2022 |
| CC-03 | SS-MPPT-60A-2214-0873 | Sub-field C (West) | 15 March 2022 |

CC-03 was installed three days after the first two because the mounting
bracket for the west array had to be re-fabricated on site. The original
bracket supplied with the unit did not match the rail profile of the west
array mounting structure. The re-fabrication was done by the site
fabrication team and the controller was mounted without further issues.

All three controllers are configured for a 48 V battery bank with the
following set points:

- Absorption voltage: 57.6 V
- Float voltage: 54.4 V
- Equalization voltage: 60.0 V (manual only, disabled by default)
- Low voltage disconnect: 44.0 V
- Low voltage reconnect: 48.0 V

The controllers communicate with the central monitoring system via
Modbus RTU over RS-485. The RS-485 bus is daisy-chained from CC-01 to CC-02
to CC-03 and then to the data logger. The bus is terminated at both ends
with 120 ohm resistors. The termination resistors were installed at the
factory for CC-01 and at the data logger end. The communication settings
are 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.

The firmware version on all three controllers was updated to version 2.1.4
on 5 September 2023. The update was performed by the site technician using
the manufacturer's USB programming cable. The update was done to address a
minor bug in the float voltage regulation that was reported by the
manufacturer. The update was successful on all three units and no further
issues have been reported.

**4.5.5 Monitoring System**

The central monitoring system consists of a data logger, a local display
unit, and a remote access gateway. The data logger is a model
DL-1000-48, serial number DL-1000-2215-0034. It is housed in a wall-mounted
enclosure in the control room, next to the main distribution panel.

The data logger records the following data at 5-minute intervals:

- PV array DC voltage and current (per sub-field)
- Battery bank voltage and current
- Charge controller status (charging, float, equalization, fault)
- Inverter AC output voltage, current, and frequency (per inverter)
- Generator run hours and fuel level (from DG1 and DG2)
- Ambient temperature and module temperature (from two sensors)

The data is stored on a local SD card (32 GB) and is also transmitted to
the remote access gateway via Ethernet. The remote access gateway is a
model RG-200, serial number RG-200-2215-0012. It is connected to the
internet via a 4G LTE modem. The gateway allows remote viewing of the
system status and alerts via the manufacturer's cloud portal.

The local display unit is a 7-inch colour touchscreen, model
TD-700, serial number TD-700-2215-0007. It is mounted on the control room
wall at eye level. The display unit shows the same data as the data logger
but in a graphical format. The display unit is powered from the 24 V DC
control circuit.

The monitoring system was installed and commissioned on 28 March 2022. The
commissioning was done by the same vendor's engineer, Mr. Tunde Adebayo,
and the site technician, Musa Ibrahim. The commissioning report is filed
under the file name "Monitoring_Commissioning_Report.pdf" in the
commissioning folder.

**5.4 Battery Bank**

The battery bank consists of 24 units of deep-cycle flooded
lead-acid batteries, model GC-200, manufactured by Deluxe Battery
Company. Each battery has a nominal voltage of 2 V and a rated capacity
of 200 Ah at the 10-hour discharge rate. The batteries are connected in
series to form a 48 V DC bus.

**5.4.1 Battery Configuration**

- Total number of batteries: 24
- Configuration: 24 series strings × 1 parallel string
- Nominal bank voltage: 48 V
- Rated bank capacity: 200 Ah (at 10-hour rate)
- Usable capacity (50% depth of discharge): 100 Ah
- Total energy storage: 9.6 kWh (at 48 V, 200 Ah)

**5.4.3 Battery Service History**

The battery bank has been serviced at regular intervals since commissioning.
The following log records all maintenance activities performed on the battery
bank. Entries are made by the technician on duty, and each entry is
initialled. The log is maintained in the control room at the Gidan Wuta
microgrid site.

**Service Log — Battery Bank (Gidan Wuta)**

| Date | Activity | Findings / Action Taken | Technician |
|------|----------|------------------------|------------|

| 10 May 2022 | Monthly check | SG readings slightly low on cells 7, 8 and 9 (1.255–1.260). Equalisation charge performed for 6 hours at 58.0 V. | A. Musa |
| 14 Jun 2022 | Monthly check | All cells within spec. Terminal torque checked and re-tightened on all 24 cells. | T. Okafor |
| 11 Jul 2022 | Monthly check | Harmattan dust noted on battery tops. Cleaned with dry cloth. No corrosion on terminals. | T. Okafor |
| 08 Aug 2022 | Monthly check | SG readings 1.275–1.285 at 28°C. Bank healthy. | A. Musa |
| 12 Sep 2022 | Monthly check | Cell 14 showing low electrolyte level. Topped up with distilled water. SG after top-up: 1.280. | T. Okafor |
| 10 Oct 2022 | Monthly check | All readings normal. Load test performed at 20 A for 30 minutes. Voltage dropped to 47.9 V, recovered to 48.5 V after rest. | A. Musa |

| 12 Dec 2022 | Monthly check | SG readings slightly high on cells 3 and 4 (1.290). Monitored, no action required. | A. Musa |

**5.4.4 Battery Replacement Notes**

During the March 2023 capacity test, cells 7, 8 and 9 were noted to have
slightly lower specific gravity readings (1.250–1.260) compared to the rest
of the bank. These cells were placed under closer observation. They were
re-charged individually and re-tested on 20 March 2023. The readings
recovered to 1.275–1.280. No replacement was deemed necessary at that time.

**5.5 Charge Controller**

The system uses one charge controller, model CC-MPPT-60, manufactured by
SolarTech Nigeria. The controller is rated for a maximum input voltage of
150 V DC and a maximum charging current of 60 A. It is configured for a
48 V battery bank.

- Model: CC-MPPT-60
- Manufacturer: SolarTech Nigeria
- Maximum PV input voltage: 150 V DC
- Maximum charging current: 60 A

**5.5.2 Charge Controller Commissioning**

The charge controller was installed and commissioned on 18 March 2022,
alongside the battery bank. The initial configuration was performed using
the front-panel buttons. The following settings were applied:

- Battery type: Flooded lead-acid
- Absorption voltage: 57.6 V
- Float voltage: 54.0 V
- Equalisation voltage: 58.0 V (manual trigger only)
- Temperature compensation: Enabled (default coefficient)
- Max charging current: 50 A (derated from 60 A to extend battery life)
